title: Colimits of simplicial categories computed as ordinary categories in each degree
statement: Use small simplicial categories and enriched functors with arbitrary object functions as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], and colimits in the universal-property sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $I$ be any small ordinary category and $D:I\to\mathrm{sCat}$ a diagram. For a simplicial category $A$ and $r\geq0$, write $A_r$ for the ordinary category with object set $\operatorname{Ob}A$ and morphism sets $A(x,y)_r$, with degree-$r$ composition. Put $O=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}\operatorname{Ob}D_i$ in sets. For every $r$, form the colimit $P_r=\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}(D_i)_r$ in small ordinary categories. The canonical map from $O$ to $\operatorname{Ob}P_r$ is a bijection. After these identifications, the simplicial operators on the $P_r$ are identity on $O$. The sets $\operatorname{Hom}_{P_r}(x,y)$, as $r$ varies, are the mapping simplicial sets of a simplicial category $P$ with object set $O$, and the induced cocone $D_i\to P$ is colimiting in $\mathrm{sCat}$. Thus evaluation $A\mapsto A_r$ preserves all small colimits, including pushouts, coproducts and sequential colimits. This statement includes the empty diagram and allows the diagram functors to identify objects.

source.place: Section 5.1, identification of simplicial categories with simplicial objects in Cat with constant objects before Definition 5.1.1; ambient colimit assertion used in the proof of Lemma 5.1.2, printed pp.27 (PDF p.27, zero-based page 26). No Stacks tag states this simplicial-enriched/constant-object comparison.

proof.text: Write $D_{i,r}=(D_i)_r$. The simplicial composition and units in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting] make each $D_{i,r}$ an ordinary category. Each enriched transition functor gives an ordinary functor in degree $r$, with the same object function in every degree. Apply [lem-coef-small-category-colimits] to obtain $P_r$ and its cocone functors $j_{i,r}:D_{i,r}\to P_r$. All indices and object and arrow sets lie in the common small universe. Only the definition of a simplicial category is taken from the interval-lifting node; none of its model-structure or cocompleteness assertions is used.

source.place: Agent argument: form the ordinary degree diagrams; ordinary colimit existence is the separately cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Construct $O$ as the quotient of $\coprod_i\operatorname{Ob}D_i$ by the equivalence relation generated by $(i,x)\sim(j,D(a)x)$ for each $a:i\to j$. A compatible family of functions out of the object sets is constant on these generating pairs, hence factors uniquely through this quotient. Thus $O$ has the required set-colimit universal property, including when the coproduct is empty. Let $o_i$ be its coprojections. The object functions of $j_{i,r}$ induce a function $c_r:O\to\operatorname{Ob}P_r$.

source.place: Tag 002U, categories-section-limit-sets, explicit quotient construction, and Tag 002F, categories-definition-colimit.

proof.text: For any small set $X$, define $K(X)$ to have object set $X$ and exactly one arrow from each object to each object, with its forced identities and composition. Every function $\operatorname{Ob}B\to X$ extends uniquely to a functor $B\to K(X)$. The functions $o_i$ therefore give a cocone $D_{i,r}\to K(O)$; its unique extension is a functor $q_r:P_r\to K(O)$. Its object function satisfies $(q_r)_{\mathrm{Ob}}c_r=1_O$, since this equality holds after every $o_i$ and the quotient map is surjective. To check the other composite, consider the two functors $P_r\to K(\operatorname{Ob}P_r)$ with object functions $c_r(q_r)_{\mathrm{Ob}}$ and $1$. Their composites with every $j_{i,r}$ agree on objects, because $(q_r)_{\mathrm{Ob}}(j_{i,r})_{\mathrm{Ob}}=o_i$ and $c_ro_i=(j_{i,r})_{\mathrm{Ob}}$; their arrow maps then agree by uniqueness of arrows in $K(\operatorname{Ob}P_r)$. The colimit uniqueness property makes the two functors equal. Consequently $c_r(q_r)_{\mathrm{Ob}}=1$, so $c_r$ is a bijection. Replace $P_r$ by the isomorphic category with objects $O$, hom sets $\operatorname{Hom}_{P_r}(c_rx,c_ry)$, and the original composition and identities. The isomorphism sends $x$ to $c_rx$ and is the identity on these hom sets; its inverse uses $c_r^{-1}$ on objects. Compose each cocone leg with this inverse. If $F$ is this isomorphism to the old $P_r$, compose its old mediating functor $h$ with $F$ to extend any cocone on the replacement. Uniqueness follows by composing a candidate extension with $F^{-1}$ and using old uniqueness. Call the replacement $P_r$ again.

source.place: Agent argument from Tag 002F, categories-definition-colimit: two explicit applications of uniqueness to categories with singleton hom sets.

proof.text: For $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ in $\Delta$, the mapping-set operators define functors $D_i(\theta):D_{i,n}\to D_{i,m}$ which are identity on objects. Naturality of the transition enriched functors makes $j_{i,m}D_i(\theta)$ a cocone on $(D_{i,n})_i$. Its unique extension is $P(\theta):P_n\to P_m$, characterized by $P(\theta)j_{i,n}=j_{i,m}D_i(\theta)$. Its object map is identity on $O$, since it is identity after all $o_i$. For $\phi:[l]\to[m]$, both $P(\phi)P(\theta)$ and $P(\theta\phi)$ have composite $j_{i,l}D_i(\theta\phi)$ with every $j_{i,n}$; the colimit uniqueness property makes them equal. For the identity operator, $P(1)j_{i,n}=j_{i,n}D_i(1)=j_{i,n}=1_{P_n}j_{i,n}$ for every $i$; colimit uniqueness gives $P(1)=1_{P_n}$. Thus these are strictly functorial simplicial operators.

source.place: Agent argument from Tag 002F, categories-definition-colimit: define operators by the universal property and check the two functor identities after all cocone legs.

proof.text: For $x,y\in O$ set $P(x,y)_r=\operatorname{Hom}_{P_r}(x,y)$ and use the restrictions of $P(\theta)$ as its simplicial operators. Step 4 gives precisely the functor identities in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Composition is composition in each $P_r$. It commutes with all operators because $P(\theta)$ is an ordinary functor: $P(\theta)(gf)=P(\theta)(g)P(\theta)(f)$. The units are the identity arrows in every degree; $P(\theta)(1_x)=1_x$ preserves them. Associativity and both unit laws hold degree by degree since $P_r$ is a category. This is exactly a simplicial category in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. For $a,b\in\operatorname{Ob}D_i$ and $f\in D_i(a,b)_n$, step 4 gives $P(\theta)(j_{i,n}f)=j_{i,m}(D_i(\theta)f)$, so the maps $j_{i,r}$ on each hom set are simplicial with common object function $o_i$. Each preserves composition and units because it is an ordinary functor. Hence they define enriched functors $j_i:D_i\to P$. For $a:i\to k$, the degreewise cocone equations $j_{k,r}D(a)_r=j_{i,r}$ give equality on objects and every hom degree, proving the enriched cocone equation $j_kD(a)=j_i$.

source.place: Agent definition check: the degreewise categorical composition and identities give the enriched structure, without a separate constant-object comparison theorem.

proof.text: Let $b_i:D_i\to B$ be any enriched cocone. For each $r$ its degree-$r$ cocone has a unique extending functor $h_r:P_r\to B_r$. The object functions of all $h_r$ are the same function $h:O\to\operatorname{Ob}B$, since each is uniquely determined by $h\,o_i=\operatorname{Ob}b_i$. For $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, compare $B(\theta)h_n$ and $h_mP(\theta)$ as functors $P_n\to B_m$. Their restrictions along $j_{i,n}$ coincide by simplicial naturality of $b_i$, so they are equal by colimit uniqueness. Restricting this equality to each hom set shows that the maps $(h_r)_{x,y}$ form simplicial maps. They preserve composition and units because each $h_r$ does. They therefore define an enriched functor $P\to B$ extending the given cocone. Any second extension has the same degree-$r$ functors by the ordinary colimit uniqueness property, hence the same object map and all the same mapping-set maps. This proves the enriched colimit universal property.

source.place: Agent argument from Tag 002F, categories-definition-colimit: construct the mediating functor in every degree and prove its simplicial compatibility by equality after the cocone legs.

proof.text: The constructed enriched colimit has degree-$r$ cocone equal to the chosen ordinary colimit cocone. For any other enriched colimit $Q$, uniqueness gives mutually inverse enriched functors $P\to Q$ and $Q\to P$ commuting with the cocones: their composites are identities by the same uniqueness property. Taking degrees gives inverse ordinary functors commuting with the degree cocones, so $Q_r$ is also an ordinary colimit. Thus evaluation preserves all the stated small colimits. If $I$ is empty, $O$ and every $P_r$ are empty (step 3), giving the empty enriched category. If transition functors identify objects, the quotient in step 2 makes those identifications and the later arguments use no object-injectivity assumption. Pushouts, coproducts and sequential diagrams are the indicated special shapes of $I$.

source.place: Agent argument from Tag 002F, categories-definition-colimit: uniqueness up to an actual isomorphism of colimit cocones and its evaluation in each degree.
